name: User Types (9 roles)
note: 9 roles; the research evidences at most 4 as buyers (IIC coordinator, incubation manager, TTO/IP officer, evaluator). Phase 2 mapped 25 roles but found 0 with documented budget authority. Founder, mentor, investor, corporate and resource-provider roles are all DEFERRED.

name: Startup Onboarding
note: Feeds differentiator 3 - the venture record must exist before incorporation.

name: Idea Management
note: Feeds GAP-09 and Phase 1's 843-ideas-from-42-activities finding.

name: Idea Validation
note: Reasonable, no competitor builds it, but nothing in 11 phases evidences demand and it is a founder-side module, not the institutional buyer.

name: Incubation Management
note: 21 of 40 build incubation natively, 11 partially. Rule 1 applies. Must be built well; cannot be the wedge.

name: Mentor Management
note: 15 of 40 native. Mentorship is even sold as a paid add-on by incuTrack. Only the NDA-tiered visibility half of GAP-07 survives.

name: IPR Management
note: Differentiator 2. The full discovery-to-licence workflow is a v2 expansion of the joined-venture record.

name: Resource Management
note: Only 3 of 40 build it natively, so the gap is real - but Phase 5 concluded we should NOT compete here: incuTrack and EcoSync are strong and this is most likely a free defensive feature, not a wedge.

name: Market Intelligence
note: Startup-side analytics. 27 of 40 build analytics; market intel is 7 native / 15 partial. Real gap, wrong buyer.

name: Competitor Intelligence
note: Founder-side. Would require the data this study itself collects. Interesting but not this buyer.

name: Product / MVP Management
note: No evidence in 11 phases. Founder-side.

name: Customer Management
note: No evidence. Founder-side.

name: Funding
note: Scheme-eligibility matching is the second half of differentiator 1. A plain grant LIST is saturated (11 of 40 native) - matching is not.

name: Fundraising Management
note: Investor-side. Not this buyer.

name: Growth Management
note: Startup-side. No evidence.

name: Startup Performance Dashboard
note: 28 of 40 build reporting, 27 analytics. Rule 1 retires this as a differentiator.

name: Risk Management
note: Plausible and connected to the TRL object, but Phase 11 found no user asking for risk scoring. Cannot be scoped without interviews.

name: Founder AI Assistant
note: Phase 11: zero users asked for AI, and 'AI assistant' is exactly the positioning Phase 11 declined to make. Keep as an internal surface over the TRL object, never as a differentiator.

name: Incubator / Accelerator (portfolio)
note: Portfolio view is standard in 15+ vendors.

name: Program Management
note: Cohort and programme management is the most built capability in the category.

name: Portfolio Dashboard
note: See #16.

name: Incubator Resource Management
note: Same reasoning as #8 - real gap, wrong strategic choice.

name: Mentor / Expert
note: Retained only for the NDA-tiered visibility half (GAP-07).

name: IPR / Legal Professional
note: Second persona for differentiator 2; expand after the venture record ships.

name: Investor
note: Investor-side. Not this buyer.

name: Investor Due Diligence
note: Investor-side.

name: Investment Management
note: Investor-side.

name: Government / Institution
note: The mandate and accreditation-return surface is the commercial reason the IIC budget exists. Note GAP-03 is now CONTESTED.

name: Government → Startup Matching
note: Same object as differentiator 1's scheme mapping, seen from the government side.

name: Resource Provider
note: Marketplace-side.

name: Resource Marketplace
note: Two-sided marketplace economics, months of work, zero evidence of demand.

name: Corporate / Industry Partner
note: Phase 9 found corporate_match is 5 native / 18 partial - mostly weak. No evidence the university buyer wants this in v1.

name: Corporate Pilot Management
note: Same reasoning as #32.

name: University / Research Institution
note: This IS the buyer. Research-to-IP-to-startup connection is differentiator 2.

name: Talent / Professional
note: Marketplace-side.

name: StartupHub Admin
note: Governance, audit logs and permissions are load-bearing for the accreditation argument and for GAP-08's auditable posture.

name: Verification & Trust Layer
note: Required for the institutional-defensibility wedge; a committee buying a system of record needs to know who certified each record.

name: Communication Layer
note: Every vendor has email, chat and reminders. Phase 11's one real complaint - email to spam - is a deliverability problem, not a feature gap.

name: Document & Knowledge Management
note: Needed eventually, not differentiating, and heavily commoditised.

name: Notification & Alert Engine
note: Standard across the category.

name: The Central AI Engine
note: As positioning, contradicted by Phase 11. As internal infrastructure, fine - but it must never be the reason a customer buys.

name: AI Matching Engine
note: Mentor matching is saturated and unasked-for. Grant/mentor matching tied to TRL is differentiator 1 and IS evidenced. Only the evidenced use ships.

name: AI Scoring Engine
note: Eight proposed scores, none evidenced. EcoSync's refusal to publish AI scores and VentureLink's actor-reason audit trail are the two data points that matter, and both are about auditability rather than the score.

name: Ecosystem Intelligence
note: Requires cross-institution data nobody has shared. Not reachable by a single institution's purchase.

name: 12-module platform structure
note: The module taxonomy is sound as architecture. As a delivery plan for v1 it is 12x too large for the evidence. Triaged at module level in MODULES_MAP.

name: Per-role distinct experiences
note: The strongest idea in features.md, and the one Phase 2 independently converged on: the IIC coordinator's question is 'which startup needs intervention', not 'show me the list'. Build the surfaces around that question.
